one_liner: Customer service suite: ticketing, help center, messaging, voice and AI agents.
auth_notes: OAuth access tokens sent as Bearer (recommended); a token only works on the instance whose OAuth client issued it. Apps distributed to multiple customers must use global OAuth tokens. API tokens (Basic with {email}/token:{api_token}) are labeled deprecated and existing customers must migrate to OAuth. End-user email/password only in closed instances where an admin enables it. Per-subdomain base URL.
access_notes: Anyone can start a 14-day Support or Sell trial and create a local OAuth client. Multi-customer distribution needs a global OAuth client that developers cannot create themselves: request it via the Marketplace portal from a d3v- subdomain; Zendesk approves and may restrict scopes. Non-expiring sponsored accounts (up to 5 agents, Suite Enterprise) are reserved for Marketplace developers via a request form.
api_breadth_notes: Many product APIs: Support/Ticketing, Help Center, Conversations, Talk, Chat, Custom Objects, Sell (plus Sync/Firehose/Search), AI Agents, Apps/ZIS, Status, Webhooks; hundreds of operations.
mcp_notes: Zendesk MCP server via Zendesk Bridge (External AI EAP): hosted at https://{subdomain}.zendesk.com/mcp; OAuth (Zendesk global client for pre-built providers, or bring-your-own OAuth client). Read and write tools (tickets, users, orgs, help center, macros; writes need human confirmation). Early access, free during EAP; Suite Team+ or Support Team+.
blocker: Multi-tenant OAuth needs Zendesk-approved global OAuth client
notes: API token auth is being deprecated in favor of OAuth, so build on OAuth (refresh tokens supported). Trial/sponsored account details: https://developer.zendesk.com/documentation/api-basics/getting-started/getting-a-trial-or-sponsored-account-for-development/ (fetched). The originally guessed trial/sandbox doc URL returned 404. Webhooks: a Webhooks section exists in the API reference sidebar; not opened in detail. MCP is EAP; packaging may change at GA.

one_liner: AI-first customer service platform: Fin AI agent, shared inbox, messenger, help center.
auth_notes: Access tokens (Bearer) for your own workspace/private apps, obtained by creating an app in the Developer Hub. OAuth is required for public apps that access other workspaces' data. Regional hosts (US/EU/AU).
access_notes: Free developer workspaces (unlimited count; US region only; max 20 users/leads; no outbound email/push; cannot become production) give self-serve access tokens. Any app installable on other workspaces, listed or unlisted, must be reviewed and approved by Intercom (up to 7 business days).
api_breadth_notes: REST API v2.18 with about 31 resource groups (contacts, conversations, companies, articles, tickets, data attributes, events, etc.).
mcp_notes: Hosted remote server: https://mcp.intercom.com/mcp (US), https://mcp.eu.intercom.com/mcp (EU); SSE endpoints deprecated; AU workspaces not supported. OAuth (recommended) or bearer token. 16 core tools (12 read; writes limited to create/update article and add internal note) plus 5 Fin Operator tools (OAuth only).
blocker: Public OAuth app requires Intercom review before other workspaces install
notes: Developer workspace details from https://developers.intercom.com/docs/build-an-integration/getting-started/. Webhook topics are subscribed per app in the Developer Hub, not via API (https://developers.intercom.com/docs/webhooks). The official MCP cannot send customer-visible replies, so the REST API is needed for a full toolkit. Changes to an approved app require re-approval.

one_liner: Freshworks help desk: omnichannel ticketing, knowledge base and automations.
auth_notes: Per-agent API key sent via HTTP Basic (key as username, any dummy password). No OAuth authorization flow is documented for the REST API v2 (Freshworks OAuth applies to Marketplace apps), though the API reference shows OAuth-style scope names on endpoints. Per-account base URL https://{domain}.freshdesk.com/api/v2.
access_notes: 14-day self-serve trial with Enterprise features (trial accounts capped at 50 API calls/min). Paid plans Growth $19, Pro $55, Enterprise $89 per agent/month (annual). A 2020 support article says the free (Sprout) plan excludes API access; the current free plan's API status was not confirmed.
api_breadth_notes: About 37 top-level categories (tickets, conversations, contacts, companies, agents, groups, solutions, automations, SLA, time entries, audit log, etc.).
mcp_notes: Freshworks-hosted MCP at https://{subdomain}.freshdesk.com/mcp (custom domains unsupported); API key in Authorization header; GA since 10 Sep 2026. Growth/Pro/Enterprise with rate limits (25/50/100 actions per min) and annual action quotas (1,200/6,000/12,000). Read and write tools (tickets, replies, notes, contacts, companies, solutions).
blocker: API-key only; paid plan needed after 14-day trial
notes: Toolkit must collect API key plus subdomain per user (no end-user OAuth). Webhooks are outbound only via automation-rule 'Trigger webhook' actions, not a subscription API (https://support.freshdesk.com/en/support/solutions/articles/50000009511-automation-examples-using-webhooks). Rate limits are account-wide per plan (Growth 100, Pro 400, Enterprise 700/min per Freshworks limits article). Sandbox is an Enterprise-plan feature.

one_liner: Collaborative shared inbox for email, SMS, chat and social customer communication.
auth_notes: Core API uses Bearer tokens: admin-created company API tokens (own instance or testing) or OAuth tokens. Public integrations for all Front customers must use OAuth unless Front grants an exception. Users authorizing OAuth apps must be admins.
access_notes: Free developer account (developer signup link; no production data; max 3 teammates; no expiry stated). Apps are private to the creating instance by default; publishing to all customers requires submitting the integration form and passing Front's technical (and possibly security/legal) review.
api_breadth_notes: Core API (conversations, messages, contacts, accounts, inboxes, channels, tags, teammates, etc.) plus Channel API, Plugin SDK, Connectors, Links, Chat Widget; exact endpoint count not verified.
mcp_notes: Hosted remote server https://mcp.frontapp.com/mcp (Streamable HTTP); OAuth 2.1 without dynamic client registration, so clients need client ID/secret from a developer app with the MCP feature; scopes read/write/send. Tools cover search/read conversations, drafts, send, assign, tag, comments, tasks, contacts. Separate Admin MCP server for settings. Rate limits 100/200/300 tool calls per min by plan.
blocker: Multi-tenant OAuth app needs Front partner review to publish
notes: Published apps cannot be edited directly; create a new app to test changes and notify Front. Server limit 1,200 req/min for apps (https://dev.frontapp.com/docs/create-and-manage-apps.md). Front may refuse integrations it sees as revenue-competitive or low quality. Webhooks available as app webhooks and rule webhooks.

one_liner: B2B support platform for Slack, Teams, email and chat with AI agents.
auth_notes: REST API uses Bearer API tokens created by Admins (Settings > Integrations & dev > API); non-expiring, role-based (no scopes), optional IP allowlist; US (api.usepylon.com) and EU (api.eu.usepylon.com) hosts. OAuth 2.0 is documented only for the hosted MCP server; no public OAuth app flow found for the REST API.
access_notes: No free plan; free trials exist only when set up by a sales rep (demo request). REST API, webhooks and MCP are included on every paid plan (Professional $89, Advanced $139 per seat/month annual; Enterprise custom). Sandbox is Enterprise-only.
api_breadth_notes: 23 resource groups (accounts, contacts, issues, messages, knowledge base, tasks/projects, custom objects, surveys, tags, teams, users, etc.).
mcp_notes: Pylon-hosted Streamable HTTP server: https://mcp.usepylon.com (US), https://mcp.eu.usepylon.com (EU); OAuth 2.0 for interactive clients or API token as Bearer for headless use; requires 'MCP Access' permission. Broad read/write tools (issues, replies, KB, tasks, accounts, analytics, webhooks, etc.).
blocker: No self-serve signup; trial only via sales
notes: Pricing and per-plan inclusions from https://www.usepylon.com/pricing. Webhooks are sent via triggers with a 'Send webhook' action (signed). For end users the toolkit likely needs an admin-created API token, or should reuse the MCP OAuth flow.

one_liner: Multichannel help desk: ticketing, live chat, call center and social inboxes.
auth_notes: API v3 keys created by admins (Configuration > System > API) with per-key permissions, sent in an 'apikey' header; v1 and v3 keys are separate. Per-tenant domain (*.ladesk.com or custom). The official OpenAPI-generated Python client also declares OAuth2 (accessCode) with scopes; the MCP server supports OAuth 2.1 + PKCE. No public docs found on registering third-party OAuth clients for the REST API.
access_notes: 30-day free trial, no credit card; no free plan. API included on every plan with API key limits (Starter 1, Team 5, Business 10, Enterprise unlimited). Regular prices from $15/agent/month (annual).
api_breadth_notes: About 39 resource groups and roughly 220 endpoints in the official Python client (tickets, calls, chats, contacts, companies, agents, departments, tags, grid, etc.).
mcp_notes: Built-in MCP server at https://{liveagent-domain}/api/mcp (Streamable HTTP); OAuth 2.1 (auth code + PKCE) or personal bearer tokens (max 10, 2-year expiry). Connecting external AI tools is limited to Business and Enterprise plans; calls count toward a shared AI budget. An early-preview FAQ gives a different path (/public/api/mcp).
blocker: Trial only; paid plan needed after 30 days
notes: The full API v3 reference lives only inside each account at {domain}/docs/api/v3; endpoint counts taken from https://github.com/QualityUnit/LiveAgent-api-python. Outbound webhooks via Rules engine 'HTTP request to external URL' action (https://support.liveagent.com/679034-Notification-postback-calls-to-external-applications-scripts). Regenerating a key immediately breaks clients using the old one.

one_liner: API-first B2B customer support platform with threads, Slack/Teams channels and AI.
auth_notes: Machine-user API keys with fine-grained permissions, sent as Bearer (multiple keys per machine user for rotation). An OAuth app option exists to call the API as a workspace user; the third-party OAuth app registration process was not confirmed. MCP uses OAuth requiring openid and offline_access scopes.
access_notes: 7-day free trial, no credit card; no free plan. Foundation $45, Horizon $99 per user/month (annual), Frontier custom. API, webhooks, events and MCP listed under the developer platform without a plan mapping.
api_breadth_notes: Single GraphQL endpoint (core-api.uk.plain.com/graphql/v1) with full UI parity; docs cover common operations, full schema published; MCP exposes nearly 400 tools.
mcp_notes: Hosted remote server https://mcp.plain.com/mcp; OAuth with Plain login (user's permissions); nearly 400 read/write tools (threads, replies, customers, labels, help center, workflows, SLAs). Claude Code needs mcp-remote workaround for token refresh.
blocker: Trial only (7 days); paid plan needed afterward
notes: Webhooks confirmed only by the pricing page's developer platform list. Plain recommends its MCP server over raw GraphQL for agents. If a self-serve third-party OAuth app exists, oauth2 would be the better auth_primary.

one_liner: Shared inbox help desk with knowledge base (Docs), live chat and customer profiles.
auth_notes: Inbox API 2.0 uses OAuth2 only: Authorization Code for integrations used by other Help Scout users, Client Credentials for internal use. Apps are created self-serve under Your Profile > My Apps; no approval documented. Credentials must belong to an active user. The separate Docs API uses an API key.
access_notes: Free plan exists but API access is tied to Standard, Plus and Pro (per MCP docs). Standard/Plus have a 15-day self-serve trial, no card. Standard $25, Plus $45, Pro $75 per user/month (annual).
api_breadth_notes: Inbox API 2.0: about 13 groups and around 150 endpoints (conversations, customers, inboxes, organizations, reports, users, teams, tags, webhooks, workflows) plus the Docs API.
mcp_notes: Hosted remote server https://mcp.helpscout.net/mcp; OAuth via Help Scout sign-in; GA. New connections are read-only (conversations, customers, inboxes, saved replies, users, workflows, reports, Docs with Docs API key); write tools planned. Requires a plan with API access; reports need Plus/Pro.
blocker: API needs paid plan after 15-day trial
notes: Self-serve OAuth auth-code flow with no review makes multi-tenant integration easy once a paid/trial account exists. Webhooks manageable via API (create/list/update/delete). API rate limits 200/400/800 per minute by tier per pricing page.

one_liner: Ecommerce-focused help desk unifying email, chat, social and voice with store data.
auth_notes: Private apps: API key used with account email as Basic auth username. Public apps: OAuth2 mandatory; authorize at https://{subdomain}.gorgias.com/oauth/authorize with scopes (e.g., tickets:read, customers:read). Per-account subdomain base URL.
access_notes: 7-day self-serve trial (no payment info) gives API keys for private use. Public OAuth apps appear on other accounts' app pages only after Gorgias approves the Developer Portal submission; draft apps can be tested on your own account. A longer-lived sandbox requires converting a trial via the Gorgias Partnerships team after registering a draft app.
api_breadth_notes: 24 resource groups (tickets, ticket messages, customers, macros, rules, views, tags, teams, users, integrations, voice calls, statistics, etc.).
mcp_notes: Gorgias-hosted server https://mcp.gorgias.com/mcp (optional ?gorgias_subdomain= for multiple brands); browser sign-in/consent acting as the user; any Helpdesk plan. Read and write (replies, notes, status, tags, macros, rules, AI Agent settings, Help Center drafts). Announced as open beta around May 2026; some writes gated.
blocker: Public OAuth app needs Gorgias review/approval
notes: Plans from $10/month (Starter); 7-day trial per https://www.gorgias.com/pricing. Outbound event delivery is via HTTP integrations (TicketHttpIntegration object), not a dedicated webhooks API; resource group list from https://developers.gorgias.com/llms.txt. Review must include testing instructions with a test account; review duration not stated on the fetched pages.

one_liner: Customer service platform built around a lifelong customer conversation timeline and AI.
auth_notes: Token-based Basic auth: agent email as username and API token as password. An admin grants the 'API User' permission; that user creates tokens (shown once). Tokens are unscoped. Org-specific host ({org}.gladly.com); sandbox at {org}.gladly.qa. App Platform installable apps reportedly use OAuth (third-party source, unverified).
access_notes: No published pricing, free plan or self-serve trial; demo/contact-sales only. API tokens are available to users of customer orgs who have the API User permission; no plan mapping stated.
api_breadth_notes: 21 REST resource groups (agents, conversations, customers, tasks, reports, topics, webhooks, answers, etc.) plus Lookup API, Chat SDK and App Platform.
mcp_notes: 'Gladly MCP for Claude' (closed beta): Gladly-hosted connector https://mcp.{region}.gladly.com/{org}/mcp plus Claude plugin; browser sign-in; Gladly must enable it per org. Scoped to Gladly AI configuration (agents, guides, workflows, actions, knowledge, simulator), read and write; documented for Claude only. General support-data MCPs are third-party (StackOne, Truto).
blocker: Enterprise sales-only; no self-serve account for testing
notes: gladly.com now redirects to gladly.ai. A third-party API report card (https://supergood.ai/api-report-card/gladly) said in Aug 2026 that no official MCP existed; Gladly's help center now documents the closed-beta Claude MCP (setup page https://help.gladly.com/docs/set-up-the-gladly-mcp-for-claude.md). Building is feasible from public docs, but testing needs a customer or partner org; could be judged blocked if no such access is available.
